rules.rule: Any color, typography, shape, elevation, or duration comes from a system token (md.sys.*) or component token (md.comp.*) generated by frameworks/design; no literal values copied into production code.
Name tokens according to the hierarchy md.ref (raw palette) > md.sys (semantic role) > md.comp (component attribute); application code references only sys or comp, never ref.
Text and icons placed on a container role use the corresponding 'on-*' role (on-primary on primary, on-secondary-container on secondary-container, etc.); never mix two non-paired roles.
The *-container roles serve as element fills; do not use them as text or icon colors.
Reserve primary for actions and most important elements, secondary for less emphasized elements (navigation selection, rejection action), tertiary for small contrasting accents (badge, highlight).
Express surface hierarchy through the five surface-container roles (lowest, low, default, high, highest) rather than elevation tint; surface-tint is deprecated.
outline delimits interactive targets and fields (3:1 required); outline-variant serves separators and decorative borders of multi-element containers; do not reverse these uses.
Avoid *-fixed roles where contrast is critical: they remain identical in light and dark.
background/on-background and surface-variant are legacy roles; prefer surface, on-surface, and surface-container-highest.

Every theme provides light and dark schemes at three standard contrast levels (0), medium (0.5), and high (1.0), generated by Material Color Utilities from the source color; role thresholds follow MCU contrast curves.
The source color can come from the brand (static) or content/wallpaper (dynamic); in either case the scheme is recalculated by MCU, never adjusted manually role by role.
Use only the 15 styles of the typographic scale (display, headline, title, body, label × large, medium, small); no ad hoc sizes.
The emphasized variant of a style (heavier weight) highlights specific text without changing size.
Express sizes, line heights, and tracking in rem (or sp) to follow user text size settings.
Corner radii come from the shape scale (none to full); no free radii.
Use only six elevation levels 0 to 5; keep few distinct levels so shadow retains its power to draw attention.
Render elevation through shadow only when surface separation requires it; otherwise through tone shift (surface-container-*) or scrim.
The hover, focus, pressed, and dragged states are rendered by a state layer of the content color (on-* role) at fixed opacity, placed between container and content.
A disabled element applies disabled opacity to content (and a dimmed container), receives no focus, hover, or press, and need not meet contrast thresholds.
At most one element in focus state, one in pressed state, and one in dragged state at a time in a layout.
For an icon or compact control, the state layer is 40dp while the interactive target is 48dp.
Spacing taken from the base 8dp scale (with sub-units 2, 4, 6, 10, 12, 14dp); name component spacings as padding/margin/gap with leading/trailing/top/bottom positions.
Layout adapts to five window width classes (compact, medium, expanded, large, extra-large) with their margins and pane counts.
